BiblicalUsage: Shadday is the name God gave Abram when He made His covenant, I am the Almighty God, walk before me and be thou perfect. Moses heard the same name at the burning bush, that God had appeared to the patriarchs as God Almighty before His name Jehovah was known. Job wrestles with the name through his suffering, and Elihu confesses that touching the Almighty, we cannot find Him out, yet the psalm promises that whoever dwells in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Almighty is the name for God when nothing else will do, the name for the God who can do what He promises. He is excellent in power and in judgment and in plenty of justice, and He will not afflict without cause. That is why I rest under His shadow, because the Almighty who cannot be found out can still be trusted.
